chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Salat is disliked in the furs (leather garments) except for what is made in the land of Al-Hijaz, or from that which is known to have been purified (slaughtered).
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in leather garments according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the juristic status of praying in garments made from animal hides, distinguishing between general dislike (*makruh*) and specific exceptions. The exemption for leather from Al-Hijaz likely stems from its historical prevalence and purity in early Islamic practice, while the condition of known proper slaughter (*dhakalah*) ensures the material's ritual purity (*taharah*) by confirming the animal was halal. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on both the physical cleanliness and the legal status of the material used in worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Salāt is disliked in the furs except for what is made in the land of Al-Hijaz, or from that which you know it has been purified (slaughtered)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is undesirable to perform Salah (prayer) in fur except those made in al-Hijaz or that you know is properly slaughtered.’”
